newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two Russian cosmonauts complete space walk.
newsitem.headline: Two Russian cosmonauts complete space walk.

text.p: Two Russian cosmonauts from the Mir orbiting station -- Valery Korzun and Alexander Koleri -- successfully completed a six-hour space walk on Monday, a spokesman at the mission control centre said.
"They have shut the hatch again," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone. "They were outside for five hours and 57 minutes."
The two cosmonauts opened a hatch and began work at 6.54 p.m. (1554 GMT) while U.S. astronaut John Blaha stayed inside the Mir to observe and monitor his colleagues' operations.
The spokesman said during the space walk the cosmonauts installed the second section of a U.S.-made solar panel to provide power for the Mir.
"The first section was connected earlier, but it could only provide a partial power supply," he said.
The solar panel was delivered to Mir by the U.S. Atlantis space shuttle last year.
Another space walk is planned for December 9 when the panel will be switched on and tested. If successful the Mir will have a 100 percent power supply.
Blaha and his two Russian colleagues have been in orbit on Mir since September 19.
